description_ru: Объяснение смены времён года наклоном земной оси.
text:
Many people think that summer happens when the Earth is closer to the sun, and winter happens when it is farther away. This idea sounds logical, but it is wrong. In fact, the Earth is closest to the sun in early January, when it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere.

The real reason for the seasons is the tilt of the Earth's axis. Our planet spins around an imaginary line that goes through the North and South Poles. This line is not straight up and down. It is tilted by about twenty-three and a half degrees. As the Earth travels around the sun, which takes one year, the same tilt always points in the same direction in space.

Because of this, the Northern Hemisphere leans towards the sun for part of the year. During that time, sunlight hits the ground more directly, the days are longer, and the weather becomes warmer. Six months later, the Northern Hemisphere leans away from the sun. The light is weaker, the days are shorter, and winter arrives. At the same moment, it is summer in the Southern Hemisphere.

Near the equator, the tilt makes little difference, so the temperature stays almost the same all year. If the Earth had no tilt, there would be no seasons at all, and every day would be very similar to the one before.

questions.question: When is the Earth closest to the sun?
How much is the Earth's axis tilted?
questions.answer: About twenty-three and a half degrees.

questions.question: Why are there almost no seasons near the equator?
questions.answer: The tilt makes little difference there.
